nodeData.topic: Fuel-free: replacing what we burn — index (draft)
nodeData.note: A study library for renewable and eco energy, for three readers: a student, a farmer or camp manager, and a minister. No set curriculum exists worldwide, so this is our own method: start from each fuel people buy and burn, show what replaces it, how ready it is and what it costs today; then the technologies, the combinations, the off-grid kit, and what to put in front of government. Nothing nuclear. Every bubble will link to an official source with the date checked; costs in KES and USD with the date. This is the INDEX ONLY — the shape of the library for KKD and his father to review before any map is written. Idea and direction: KKD's father (30 Oct and 1 Nov 2026). (Checked 2 Nov 2026.)

children.topic: A · What burns today, what replaces it
children.note: One branch per use of a bought fuel. Each bubble will carry: today's fuel and its cost per unit of useful energy (KES and USD), the alternatives, readiness (lab / pilot / market), cost today, and who sells it in Kenya, Africa, the world. Anchored on IEA and IPCC categories so a government reader recognises them. (Checked 2 Nov 2026.)

children.topic: A1 · Why: what we burn and what it costs
children.note: Petrol, diesel, kerosene, charcoal, firewood, LPG: how much a household, a farm and the country spend; what each gives in useful energy; the health and forest cost. Kenya numbers from EPRA and the Ministry of Energy; world numbers from IEA. (Checked 2 Nov 2026.)

Cars, boda-boda, matatu, trucks. Petrol/diesel → electric two-wheelers, e-buses, biofuel, hydrogen (carrier only). Kenya cases as examples with dates, no endorsements. Cost per km today vs fuel. (Checked 2 Nov 2026.)

Charcoal, kerosene, LPG → electric pressure cookers, biogas, ethanol, solar cookers, improved biomass stoves. 68% of Kenyans still cook on traditional fuels (KNeCS). Kenya National Cooking Transition Strategy 2024–2028 and Clean Cooking Alliance data. (Checked 2 Nov 2026.)

children.topic: A4 · Farm pumps and small business
children.note: Diesel pumps and generators → solar pumps, solar mini-grids, ram pumps (see B-without-electricity). Cost per hour of pumping; payback years. (Checked 2 Nov 2026.)
Diesel gensets for homes, clinics, shops → solar + battery, grid + battery with net metering. Cost per kWh of backup today. (Checked 2 Nov 2026.)
Boilers and kilns on fuel oil, biomass → solar thermal, biogas, heat pumps, efficiency. Where heat is the real need, not electricity. (Checked 2 Nov 2026.)
Kerosene lamps and dry cells → solar lanterns and pay-as-you-go solar home systems, the Kenyan success story; what it costs per month today. (Checked 2 Nov 2026.)

children.topic: B · Technologies — how each works, numbers, where it fits, limits
children.note: One bubble per technology. Each will carry: how it works in plain words, efficiency, cost per kWh (IRENA/Lazard/NREL, dated), lifetime, where it fits, limits. Readiness marked proven / pilot / claim. (Checked 2 Nov 2026.)
Panels to electricity. Cheapest new electricity in most of the world in 2024 (IRENA); daytime only, so storage or a partner source for night. (Checked 2 Nov 2026.)
Sun to heat: water heaters, cookers, dryers, concentrating plants. Often the cheapest way to replace a burned fuel where heat is the need. (Checked 2 Nov 2026.)
Onshore turbines, small wind for farms; Kenya's Lake Turkana wind farm as the national example; variable, often strongest at night — a natural partner to solar. (Checked 2 Nov 2026.)
Four separate bubbles, because they are different machines with different limits. (Checked 2 Nov 2026.)
Pilot stage worldwide; predictable (tides) but costly; limits for Kenya's coast. (Checked 2 Nov 2026.)
Small turbines in a flowing river; cheap and quick; depends on the dry season. (Checked 2 Nov 2026.)
Already lighting villages in the Kenyan highlands; sizing from head and flow; community-run. (Checked 2 Nov 2026.)

children.topic: B4d · Large dam hydro and its limits
children.note: Kenya's hydro share and its drought risk; silting, displacement, climate dependence. (Checked 2 Nov 2026.)
Kenya's leading source — about 40–41% of electricity generated in 2024/25 and 2025/26 (EPRA). Steady day and night; where the Rift Valley allows it. (Checked 2 Nov 2026.)
Dung, crop waste and food waste to gas for cooking and power; biomass stoves and boilers. Hard truth: biomass vs food land. (Checked 2 Nov 2026.)
Anaerobic digestion, gasification, incineration with heat recovery; scrap and waste as fuel because waste is abundant. Hard truth: air quality rules and sorting. (Checked 2 Nov 2026.)

children.topic: B8 · Hydrogen — a carrier, not a source
children.note: Made from electricity or gas, stored, burned or used in fuel cells; flagged as a carrier; cost and losses today. (Checked 2 Nov 2026.)

Batteries by chemistry (lithium-ion, LFP, sodium-ion, flow), flywheel, pumped hydro, thermal store, compressed air, gravity. Each: duration, cycle life, cost per kWh, with dates (DOE Energy Storage Handbook; IRENA: utility battery cost down 93% from 2010 to 2024). (Checked 2 Nov 2026.)

children.topic: B9a · Flywheel — the first worked question
children.note: Published work: flywheels are best for high power, many cycles, seconds-to-hours balancing; self-discharge limits overnight storage (Sandia ESHB ch. 7). The map must say this and link both sides. (Checked 2 Nov 2026.)
National grid, mini-grids, pay-as-you-go solar; Kenya's mini-grid rules and net metering (see E). (Checked 2 Nov 2026.)
The cheapest kilowatt-hour is the one not used: lighting, cooking, motors, buildings; Kenya National Energy Efficiency Strategy. (Checked 2 Nov 2026.)

children.topic: B12 · Magnets — where they work and where they don't
children.note: Permanent-magnet generators (wind, hydro, flywheel), magnetic bearings (cut flywheel losses), maglev, magnetic refrigeration. Plain note: energy from magnets alone ("free energy" motors, perpetual motion) breaks conservation of energy and no device has ever passed an independent test. A student should be able to answer that question from this bubble. (Checked 2 Nov 2026.)

children.topic: B13 · Energy without electricity (added at his request)
children.note: Placed next to D because for a farm or a camp it is often the cheapest answer. Each: how it works, what it replaces, KES cost, where to buy or build, limits. (Checked 2 Nov 2026.)
Water's own flow lifts a share of itself uphill; no fuel; ~200 years old; still made in Kenya. Replaces a diesel pump where there is a drop in the stream. (Checked 2 Nov 2026.)
Channels and pipes using the land's slope; no pump at all. (Checked 2 Nov 2026.)

children.topic: Solar water heaters and solar cookers
children.note: Heat without a flame; replaces kerosene and charcoal for hot water and slow cooking. (Checked 2 Nov 2026.)
Shade, ventilation, clay-pot coolers: cold without a compressor. (Checked 2 Nov 2026.)
Mechanical pumping; the classic farm windpump and the human-powered treadle pump. (Checked 2 Nov 2026.)
Cooking gas from waste; water circulating by heat alone. (Checked 2 Nov 2026.)
Pairs and triples: what each solves, "evidence for", "evidence against", "open question", with dated links. Research feed lands here. (Checked 2 Nov 2026.)
Sun by day, wind often by night; how much storage the pair still needs. (Checked 2 Nov 2026.)

children.topic: C2 · Generation + flywheel for the night
children.note: The first worked example. For: seconds-to-hours smoothing, long life, no chemicals. Against: self-discharge overnight. Open question: can a low-loss flywheel with magnetic bearings carry a household to morning? The map tests the idea rather than assumes it. (Checked 2 Nov 2026.)
Gas for the flame, solar for the electric cooker; what a household of six needs. (Checked 2 Nov 2026.)
Keep the heat from a kiln or engine in sand, salt or water for later. (Checked 2 Nov 2026.)
The Kenyan urban case under the 2024 net-metering rules: size, payback, limits. (Checked 2 Nov 2026.)
River in the wet season, sun in the dry: a highland village mix. (Checked 2 Nov 2026.)

children.topic: C7 · Research feed (dated, one bubble each)
children.note: Daily run adds new papers and reports — IRENA, IEA, NREL/ATB, arXiv energy, open-access journals — tagged "new · unreviewed" under the right spine. (Checked 2 Nov 2026.)

Any "generates without top-up" or breakthrough claim, from anywhere, goes here within a day with its source, date and one of three marks: peer-reviewed / independently tested; company or state announcement, no independent test; claim only. Real advances (perovskite solar, sodium-ion batteries, cheap flow batteries) land as evidence; free-energy claims land as unverified. Nothing hidden, nothing endorsed without a test. Thorium and other nuclear: out of scope, noted only. (Checked 2 Nov 2026.)

children.topic: D · Off-grid kit for a home, a clinic, a camp
children.note: Sizing, bill of materials, KES cost, where parts come from, what fails first. Fit for UNHCR / Red Cross field practice (Clean Energy Challenge, Global Platform for Action). (Checked 2 Nov 2026.)
Lights, phones, a fridge, an electric cooker: daily kWh, panel and battery size, cost today, payback vs kerosene and charcoal. (Checked 2 Nov 2026.)
Vaccine fridge, lights, lab equipment, a maternity ward at night: what must never go off; sizing with a margin. (Checked 2 Nov 2026.)

children.topic: D3 · A camp block of N people
children.note: Lighting, water pumping, cooking, phone charging for a block; the UNHCR energy approach; what has worked in Kakuma and Dadaab (dated). (Checked 2 Nov 2026.)

children.topic: D4 · Bill of materials and suppliers
children.note: Panels, inverter, batteries, cables, mounts, meters: where they are made, who sells in Kenya, warranty years. (Checked 2 Nov 2026.)
Batteries, inverters, charge controllers, dust and theft; maintenance plan and spares. (Checked 2 Nov 2026.)
The house designed around its own energy: orientation, solar roof, water heating, cooking — toward the UN / Red Cross camp and the rural home. (Checked 2 Nov 2026.)

children.topic: E · Policy and the proposal to government
children.note: What a minister or a county needs to see, drawn from spines A and D as a one-page map. (Checked 2 Nov 2026.)

Geothermal ~41%, hydro, wind, solar, thermal and imports (EPRA statistics 2024/25 and 2025/26) — already among the greenest grids; where the gaps are (peak, drought years, rural access). (Checked 2 Nov 2026.)
Licences, tariffs, who may generate and sell; the regulator's statistics and tariff pages. (Checked 2 Nov 2026.)
Legal Notice 104 of 2024: systems under 1 MW may bank surplus on the grid; what a school, hospital or factory can do today. (Checked 2 Nov 2026.)
How a village or camp mini-grid is licensed and priced; pay-as-you-go. (Checked 2 Nov 2026.)
National target of universal clean cooking by 2028 (KNCTS); the electric-cooking strategy; what the state offers and what it still lacks. (Checked 2 Nov 2026.)
What a county government can do without Nairobi: pumps, clinics, street lighting, waste-to-energy at the dump. (Checked 2 Nov 2026.)
For a minister: the three fuels to replace first, the cost today, the payback, the jobs, the pilot sites — drawn from A and D. (Checked 2 Nov 2026.)

children.topic: E8 · Hard truths to state up front
children.note: Storage cost, intermittency, waste-to-energy air quality, biomass vs food land, import dependence for panels and batteries. (Checked 2 Nov 2026.)
Official sources every bubble will link to, so the library is credible without a syllabus. (Checked 2 Nov 2026.)
Global energy system, scenarios, technology categories. (Checked 2 Nov 2026.)

children.topic: IRENA Renewable Power Generation Costs in 2024 (June 2025)
children.note: Costs per technology, yearly, free; 91% of new renewable capacity cheaper than the cheapest new fossil option. (Checked 2 Nov 2026.)
Public-domain cost and performance data for generation and storage. (Checked 2 Nov 2026.)
Levelised cost of energy and storage, yearly. (Checked 2 Nov 2026.)

children.topic: IPCC AR6 WG3 chapter 6 — Energy systems
children.note: The reference chapter on the whole energy transition. (Checked 2 Nov 2026.)
Kenya's generation mix, tariffs, petroleum prices. (Checked 2 Nov 2026.)
Storage technologies chapter by chapter, incl. flywheels. (Checked 2 Nov 2026.)
Energy in displacement settings; field practice for camps. (Checked 2 Nov 2026.)

Own words only; link + date on every bubble; costs in KES and USD dated; readiness marked; three audiences, labels readable aloud; nothing nuclear; no endorsements; reviewer (energy engineer; for camps, UNHCR Kenya or Red Cross) before the maps leave draft. (Checked 2 Nov 2026.)
